gen-gf-cherry-swash-gf-ojuju: Ojuju flexes gently from thick to thin, like a lightly bent spring wire. And Cherry Swash holds one heavy, wire-like line throughout, with a horseshoe c, while the body does its best work in that soft ebb.
gen-gf-cherry-swash-gf-philosopher: Cherry Swash puts its horizontals at the same heft as its verticals, giving the heading a blunt, confident look up top. Philosopher then flows quietly, its curves roomy inside.
gen-gf-cherry-swash-gf-pt-sans: Tubular, wire-like letters give Cherry Swash a look nobody could mistake for anything else. But PT Sans keeps its low-key shapes open, so the text slides by without any fuss.
gen-gf-cherry-swash-gf-teachers: Cherry Swash arrives with a wide horseshoe c and heavy diagonals. Teachers follows in thin, steel-rod lines that taper off before they touch, so the text feels light and modern.
gen-gf-cherry-swash-gf-tenor-sans: Chunky, wide-mouthed and sure of itself. Cherry Swash leads like a single thread, while Tenor Sans has gently weighted stems and lighter hairlines; a larger heading size would suit that gap.
gen-gf-cherry-swash-gf-tirra: Tirra builds its round forms like open parentheses, giving text a modern, unfussy openness with very little shading. Cherry Swash, with no pen modulation either, keeps going.
gen-gf-cherry-swash-gf-tsukimi-rounded: Cherry Swash opens its c wide like a horseshoe and draws diagonals as heavy as its verticals. But Tsukimi Rounded is the quiet one, with parallel stroke edges running smoothly through every curve.
gen-gf-cherry-swash-gf-urbanist: Urbanist moves like a rolling-ball pen, with one line that never curls shut. Cherry Swash, meanwhile, sits above it with a wide horseshoe c, so reading the text feels easy and modern.
gen-gf-cherry-swash-gf-varta: Wide, heavy and smooth, with no thick-to-thin shading at all. Varta then follows with big open eyes on every e and a, so the text stays low-contrast beneath that bold heading.
gen-gf-cherry-swash-gf-vazirmatn: Heavy, wire-like and unshaded. Cherry Swash is best when curves and straights share one width, whereas Vazirmatn does its best work with a wide-open s that never tightens in text.
